They know that they were robbed by one man, for whatever his agenda was, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors. Okay guys, major news in the Lindsay Clancy case. The mistrial is now official. After almost six weeks, the trial is over with no verdict, apparently because of one male juror. The jury heard more than 80 witnesses and saw around 300 exhibits, then spent seven days and more than 36 hours deliberating. Three times they told the judge they could not reach a unanimous verdict. Unanimous is the keyword. All 12 jurors have to agree. 11 out of 12 is still no verdict and the evidence strongly suggests that is exactly what happened. 11 jurors were ready to find Lindsay not guilty, but one juror was against it. The jury was nine women and three men. During an argument about the holdout, Lindsay's lawyer Kevin Reddington appeared to accidentally reveal that the juror was a man. He said, I would go so far as to say he lied under oath. And then, after the mistrial, Reddington said the other jurors had been robbed by one man, who stole seven weeks of the life of these other jurors. Pretty ironic for him to use the phrase, stole seven weeks of life, given that he was defending a woman who took away three lives of her kids. By the way, I think it was highly unethical and unprofessional for a defense attorney to reveal the gender of one person, who apparently was against not guilty verdict. The juror's identity were being highly protected in this case, and by revealing that the holdout was a man, Reddington effectively narrowed his identity down to one of only three male jurors. Especially in a case this high profile, where this one juror is already getting a lot of anger online, I think that was a very inappropriate thing to do. Also, here's the legal part that surprised me. I kind of thought that normally the prosecution's job would be to prove that Lindsay Clancy was guilty of killing her three kids, and then the defense's job would be to argue something like, yes, but she was psychotic. But in Massachusetts, once the defense argues that mental illness made her not criminally responsible, the defense does not actually have to prove it. Instead, the prosecution has to prove beyond a reasonable doubt that she was still criminally responsible for what she did. So in a way, that makes the prosecution's job much harder, and defense's job much easier. And this is why the fight over that one juror became so important. According to the foreperson, the holdout acknowledged having doubt, but was refusing to apply it to the verdict. The defense argued that this meant he was refusing to follow the judge's instructions on reasonable doubt, while the prosecution said it could simply be a disagreement over what actually counts as reasonable doubt. Eventually, Reddington asked the judge to remove him, but the judge refused. And after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict for the third time, the judge moved to declare a mistrial. Lindsay's defense made an emergency appeal to Massachusetts' highest court to stop it. That failed, and on September 4th, the mistrial became official. So what does that mean? Lindsay was not convicted, but she was also not acquitted. A mistrial means the trial ended without a verdict. The murder charges are still there, and prosecutors can try her again with a new jury. For now, Lindsay remains in the state psychiatric hospital. The next hearing is September 29th, and there are several possibilities. Prosecutors can retry her. The two sides can negotiate a plea deal. The defense can ask the judge to dismiss the charges or find Lindsay not guilty without another trial, although legal experts say that is a long shot. And prosecutors can also decide not to retry the case at all, although that seems unlikely. If there is a second trial, it would mean a new jury, but many of the same lawyers, witnesses, and experts could return. There's no new trial date yet, and realistically, it would probably be months away. So the first Lindsay Clancy trial is officially over, but the case itself is not.
